text:
liza (incident-bot): :rotating_light: Paging: Control plane elevated 5xx rates observed in US region (auth + org-lookup). Threshold crossed: 5m error rate > 8%. Paging oncall for incidents channel. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/controlplane-deps

sam (oncall): seeing alerts too. 5xx spike started ~10:02 UTC, hitting API gateway ~30% of requests returning 502/504. TL;DR: auth service and org-lookup returning 500s intermittently, causing upstream gateway to escalate.

anya (sre): confirming. Cloudwatch/Kuma traces show auth latencies spiking and a surge of retries to org-lookup. Some stacks show downstream timeouts at 1.5s.

mike (eng): any recent deploys to auth/org-lookup in the last 2h?

deploy-bot: deploys: auth-service v3.14.2 at 09:47 UTC by mike; org-lookup v1.7.0 at 08:55 UTC by jenny.

sam (oncall): okay deploys noted. rolling back isn't first step until we confirm repro. Can we triage impact: customer-facing API error % and number of active customers seeing errors? neha?

neha (prod-support): support queue: 12 incoming tickets in last 20m referencing 502s on API. Top affected customers: acme-corp, beta-saas. Resp time from NOC: customers seeing failed requests to user provisioning / org endpoints.

anya (sre): dashboards: gateway 5xx rate jumped from 0.4% to 7.8% at 10:02, peaked 11.2% at 10:08. Auth 500s correlate; org-lookup 500s triage shows DB errors and connection exhaustion logs.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) enable circuit-breaker / short-circuit to fallback cache for org-lookup 2) increase timeout for auth requests to reduce upstream 502s? 3) scale up auth pods (hotpath). Which is fastest?

mike (eng): fastest: flip org-lookup fallback to read-from-cache-only for 10m window (config flag). I can flip that in ~2min with a config toggle. Also will add temporary traffic split to healthy auth instances if autoscaler slow.

anya (sre): agree. Also add a client-side rate-limit on retries to auth to avoid thundering herd. Will patch proxy config to jitter retries.

sam (oncall): mike — go ahead with cache-only toggle. post the command and confirm. I'll coordinate comms and page C-level if SLA at risk.

mike (eng): running: 
```
# feature flag toggle
curl -X POST https://config-internal/flags/orglookup/cache_mode -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"mode":"cache_only","expiry":"10m"}'
```
Response: 200 OK. Flipped to cache_only at 10:14 UTC.

anya (sre): applying retry jitter: 
```
# proxy control
kubectl -n controlplane patch configmap/retry-policy --patch '{"data":{"auth_retries":"3","jitter_ms":"200-800"}}'
```
Patch applied at 10:15 UTC.

liza (incident-bot): action logged: org-lookup cache_only enabled by mike; retry-jitter applied by anya. Notifying oncall log.

sam (oncall): metrics: gateway 5xx dropped to 2.3% within 3m. Good signal. But auth still showing intermittent 500s. Need to reduce blast radius: route new traffic to a subset of auth cluster that shows healthy traces. mike, can you create a traffic-split to send 20% to older stable revision v3.13.9?

mike (eng): creating traffic split in service mesh, 20% -> v3.13.9, 80% -> v3.14.2. Command: 
```
kubectl -n auth apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: split.smi.io/v1
kind: TrafficSplit
metadata:
  name: auth-split-temp
spec:
  service: auth
  backends:
  - service: auth-v3-13-9
    weight: 20
  - service: auth-v3-14-2
    weight: 80
EOF
```
Applied at 10:18 UTC.

anya (sre): confirm traces: the older revision has far fewer 5xx traces; good. Gateway 5xx now 0.9% and trending down. Continue monitoring 10m.

neha (prod-support): routing change helped; customers reporting intermittent recovery. I posted interim status to status.redwood.com: "Degraded: API errors due to control plane dependency failures. Mitigations applied; monitoring."

sam (oncall): good. Next: deeper root cause. org-lookup logs show connection pool exhaustion to billing-db replica causing errors when certain queries spike. Any DB-level recent changes?

mike (eng): ops: running queries to inspect slow queries and pool usage. Looks like a recent config change in org-lookup increased allowed concurrent queries per worker, accidentally creating many long-running transactions. Rolling that back now.

deploy-bot: config rollback event queued for org-lookup at 10:25 UTC.

anya (sre): while rollback occurs, keep cache-only mode until 10:40 or until we confirm DB stable. Also bump healthcheck aggressiveness for auth to quickly evict unhealthy nodes.

sam (oncall): I want comms prepared: status update in 15m summarizing mitigation and ETA for full remediation. neha, can you draft?

neha (prod-support): drafting: "We are seeing elevated 5xx errors caused by third-party control plane dependencies (auth, org-lookup). We have applied fallback cache, reduced retries, and shifted some traffic to a stable auth revision. We are monitoring and expect continued recovery. Next update in 15 minutes." Will post 10:30 UTC.

mike (eng): rollback complete at 10:27 UTC. DB pool returns to normal metrics. org-lookup 500s trending down to baseline.

anya (sre): healthchecks evicted a handful of auth pods; mesh routed to healthy ones. Observability: traces show error traces mostly gone. Gateway 5xx at 0.4% now.

liza (incident-bot): automated postmortem stub created: incident-id INC-2026-0543. Recorded mitigation steps and actions.

sam (oncall): nice work. Next steps / action items: 
- mike: follow up with a config safe-guard for org-lookup pool config (PR + canary) — due EOD.
- anya: add a circuit-breaker rule to fallback to cache for repeated org-lookup 5xx within 1m.
- neha: notify top affected customers with root-cause summary and ETA.
- sam: schedule post-incident review with infra & eng next day.

mike (eng): acknowledged. I'll open PR and link it here. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/org-lookup/pull/421

neha (prod-support): status update posted at 10:30 UTC. Customers responded :thumbsup: for quick mitigation.

anya (sre): closing the live mitigation loop. Leaving org-lookup in cache_only for another 10m while we validate. Will revert to normal mode only after 30m of healthy metrics.

sam (oncall): marking incident as under control at 10:35 UTC. Logging all artifacts and artifact links: 
- traces: https://observability.redwood/traces/INC-2026-0543
- logs: https://logs.redwood/paths/controlplane/org-lookup
- runbook used: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/controlplane-deps

liza (incident-bot): incident state: under_control. Next: postmortem editor assigned to anya.

mike (eng): quick note: while this was mitigated, we should also add better client-side caching heuristics for org-lookup to reduce DB pressure during spikes. Adding to PR backlog.

neha (prod-support): closing support tickets with follow-up note.

sam (oncall): thanks everyone. Will keep channel open for 30m then archive. Great cross-team coordination.

anya (sre): leaving a short summary for postmortem: root cause = org-lookup config change that allowed long-running DB transactions; symptom = connection exhaustion -> 500s -> gateway 502/504. Mitigations = cache_only fallback, retry jitter, traffic split to stable auth, config rollback. Action items listed above.

mike (eng): saving logs and traces, will attach to PR.

liza (incident-bot): incident closed to active paging at 11:05 UTC (monitoring still active).
